question: How do on-die SRAM capacity, banking, TMA and the SRAM-side mapping move TPS/usr, and at what area and power?
status: MODEL: one-at-a-time replays of the detailed model at one design point. Changes no baseline, gate or published number

memoryLane.note: the DMA/MC lane runs in parallel with the serial chain; busy close to raw means bandwidth, not SRAM, sets the floor

localTile.check: A.mappedPlan: infeasible when usedMiB > usableMiB = capacityMiB x LIMITS.usable; usedMiB includes TECH.layoutImbalance

classes.loadBearing: an adverse move breaks the raw budget or makes the point infeasible (bearsBy says which); infeasible mappings and model errors are not counted
classes.slack: every adverse move costs < 1 TPS/usr and at least one frees die area or power
classes.insensitive: every adverse move costs < 1 TPS/usr and none frees area or power
classes.graded: adverse moves cost TPS but the budget holds
classes.basis: a counting basis (ADR-0004), not a design choice; reported, not classified
classes.untested: no adverse move on the list (the published value is the lowest step)

parameters.name: lMiB
parameters.evidence: MODEL (A.TECH SRAM density; L local tile use in criticalPath.occupancy.localTile.lCore)
parameters.measurementNeeded: SRAM macro density and energy for the target process; L-core tile footprint from the kernel mapping

parameters.name: hMiB
parameters.evidence: MODEL (A.TECH SRAM density; H local tile use in criticalPath.occupancy.localTile.hCore)
parameters.measurementNeeded: SRAM macro density; H-core tile footprint from the kernel mapping

parameters.name: sharedMiB
parameters.measurementNeeded: shared-SRAM occupancy trace (prefetch window, RDMA workspace) from an event-level replay

parameters.name: lBanks
parameters.measurementNeeded: bank-conflict counts from Palladium cycles of the L-core kernels

parameters.name: hBanks
parameters.measurementNeeded: bank-conflict counts from Palladium cycles of the H-core kernels

parameters.name: bankBytes
parameters.measurementNeeded: bank width vs access granularity from the kernel mapping

parameters.name: sharedSlices
parameters.measurementNeeded: shared-slice contention trace (NoC + port) from an event-level replay

parameters.name: tmaBytes
parameters.measurementNeeded: TMA burst size vs SRAM port width on RTL

parameters.name: kvTile
parameters.measurementNeeded: FlashMLA tile sweep on the target kernel

parameters.name: depth
parameters.measurementNeeded: DMA prefetch trace: lookahead actually reached before eviction

parameters.name: headTile
parameters.measurementNeeded: H-core tile footprint per head tile from the kernel mapping (score and accumulator bytes scale with it)

parameters.name: layoutImbalance
parameters.measurementNeeded: two roles, one factor: capacity (it scales the local tile bytes of the H/L tile check) needs the memory-compiler macro shape imbalance over every SRAM instance (VV_MEASUREMENT_PLAN.md item 6); time (it scales every kernel time) needs the per-bank access histogram from Palladium
parameters.note: slowest-bank factor on every kernel time AND on the local-SRAM tile capacity check (H local tile use in criticalPath.occupancy.localTile.hCore): too large makes the point infeasible, not just slower; ASSUMPTION

parameters.name: sharedPortScaling
parameters.measurementNeeded: event-level trace showing the mechanism engages at the published point
parameters.role: shared-SRAM write/read port scaling and dedicated TMA port, charged in area/power
parameters.note: tmaPortWriteScale multiplies the shared write port only while tmaDedicatedPort is on (O.mapped); the switch-back turns the port off, so the scale goes inert and is not patched

parameters.name: kvPrefetch
parameters.measurementNeeded: event-level trace showing the mechanism engages at the published point
parameters.role: KV context tiles of the next x.depth layers prefetched into shared SRAM
parameters.note: replayed with dmaPreempt held on: the demand fetch parks an in-flight KV prefetch; the coupling kvPrefetch off x dmaPreempt off separates the two

parameters.name: tmaLane
parameters.measurementNeeded: event-level trace showing the mechanism engages at the published point
parameters.role: shared->local fills issued ahead on per-domain (L/H) TMA lanes

parameters.name: kvCache
parameters.measurementNeeded: event-level trace showing the mechanism engages at the published point
parameters.role: FlashMLA FP8 KV layout, BF16 compute with in-kernel dequant; coupled to softmaxFusion -- the dequant runs on the H vector lanes and is charged against the softmax hiding budget, so ablating either alone understates the joint effect
parameters.note: shares the H local tile check with kvTile and the H vector lanes with softmaxFusion; see the couplings with both

provenance.profile: K3 TP32 decode / MC1152 / detailed model

constraint.comparison: candidate die area <= published die area
constraint.note: discrete SRAM/compute/communication alternatives; unused area is not silently reallocated

stressPolicy.mapping: candidate kvTile/headTile/depth preserved; not the standard pinned-kvTile stress card

softwareReschedule.constraint: only kvTile, headTile and depth are rescheduled; no additional software gain or precision change

couplings.why: both sides of the H local tile check: capacity against the KV slab bytes

couplings.name: hMiB=8 x layoutImbalance=1.3
couplings.why: layoutImbalance scales the tile bytes; more H capacity may move the point where the tile stops fitting

couplings.name: hMiB=8 x layoutImbalance=1.4
couplings.why: layoutImbalance scales the tile bytes; more H capacity may move the point where the tile stops fitting

couplings.name: hMiB=8 x kvCache off
couplings.why: bf16 KV doubles the KV slab bytes of the H tile; more H capacity may let the fallback fit at the published kvTile

couplings.name: headTile=48 x kvCache off
couplings.why: a smaller head tile frees the score / accumulator bytes that bf16 KV needs

couplings.name: hBanks=32 x layoutImbalance=1.3
couplings.why: fewer H banks and a worse slowest-bank factor both act on the H-side SRAM read time

couplings.name: hBanks=32 x layoutImbalance=1.4
couplings.why: fewer H banks and a worse slowest-bank factor both act on the H-side SRAM read time

couplings.name: hBanks=32 x layoutImbalance=1.8

couplings.name: tmaLane off x kvPrefetch off
couplings.why: the dedicated TMA lane and the KV prefetch both take shared->local traffic off the critical path

couplings.name: tmaLane off x commOverlap off
couplings.why: collectives overlap the TMA traffic; without the lane the overlap may have less to hide behind

couplings.name: sharedSlices=8 x sharedPortScaling off
couplings.why: fewer shared slices and no port scaling both cut the shared-SRAM write bandwidth

caveats: parameter rows hold mapping and OPT at the design point except the named move; tradeoffStudies.softwareReschedule separately searches mapping knobs while keeping OPT and precision fixed
die area / power are the detailed model's; at a joint point they leave out the Comm Core area (inputs.point.model.commCoreAreaMm2), which the coupling row's die area includes
moves are one step on a neighbour list (or the sweep values), not gradients; interactions appear only in jointPessimistic, the stress replays and couplings
couplings are reported, not classified: a pair that breaks the budget only together is flagged breaksOnlyTogether, the rows keep their one-at-a-time class
the stress point (JOINT_PESSIMISTIC.allUnmeasured) is an invented scenario, not a forecast
K3 / TP32 / 1M context / Batch=1 on the detailed model only; GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro have no attribution here (UNCORROBORATED)
dTpsPerMm2 / dTpsPerW are null where the move does not change die area / power
the classification is mechanical; whether a break-even lies inside the physically plausible range is decided in design.attribution, not here
